streak.note: Apple's own Turkish for this concept: 'Hareket serisi' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/MonthlyAchievements/localization/challenge/MoveStreak_SMALL_INCREASE | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_ALERT_DESCRIPTION/NSStringLocalizedFormatKey). 0 tr units exist; the 48 ro keys of this family are the scope this governs. What the list cannot cover: Turkish agglutination stacks possessive, case and plural in combination, so compounds such as 'gün serisi', 'serinizdeki' or 'serisindeki' are matched only when the exact surface form is listed; term_audit is a grep aid, not a validator. 'seri' is also the everyday adjective for 'quick', which inflates the count harmlessly.

task.note: Apple's Turkish for Task / Tasks is Görev / Görevler (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/WorkflowKit.framework | Localizable.strings | Task (OmniFocusProject); System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/DataAccess.framework | DataAccess.strings | AUTOGENERATED_MAIN_TASKS_TITLE). Governs focusTask.*, plan.*, widgets.tasks.* and insights.mood.completedTasks. 'aktivite' is deliberately not forbidden: Apple's own Screen Time copy says 'aktivite verileri' for activity data, which is correct in onboarding.screenTimePermission.* and screenTimeReport.noDataExplanation. 'iş' is not forbidden either, because 'iş günü' is the right rendering of the work-day unit in share.duration.daysSpelled.

restricted_list.note: Plain wording chosen over Apple's Settings vocabulary: Apple says 'Sınırlamalar' for Restrictions and 'Uygulama Sınırları' for App Limits (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | RestrictionsGroupSpecifierName, AppLimitsSpecifierName), but this app blocks the apps outright, and 'Engelle' is Apple's own verb for blocking (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/NewsFeed.framework | Localizable.strings | Block). Keys: screenTime.createRestrictedList.*, screenTime.restrictedAppsPicker.*, plan.createToDo.removeRestrictedApps, plan.createToDo.restrictedAppsSection. The forbidden forms are pejorative or legal-sounding, not everyday words for this list. The group name 'No Restricted Apps' ships as an unlocalized Swift literal (ToDoTaskRepository.swift:333): flag it, never translate it in place.

time_value.note: Apple's Turkish for Value is 'Değer' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ActionKit.framework | Localizable.strings | Value (WFGetDictionaryValueType)). Keys: insights.savings.*, achievements.category.wages.*, achievements.badge.*.earned, widgets.cash.*, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, onboarding.with(out)Moneyfesting.*. The outcome words are deliberately NOT in this forbidden list: every candidate stem (kazan, para, gelir) also occurs inside one of the five fixed disclaimer sentences, so banning them here would flag the frame itself. They are policed by references/locale-briefs/tr.md '## Money frame', which names each stem's collisions. 'birikim' is safe to forbid: it means accumulated money and is never right for an estimate of time, while the sanctioned 'birikir' (adds up) is a different whole word.

time_value_disclaimer.note: One target form per source form, reused verbatim on all 11 en keys that carry 'Not money earned.' (achievements.badge.*.earned x7, achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). The four sibling sentences keep their own single tr form, listed in references/locale-briefs/tr.md '## Money frame': 'Zamanın tahmini değeri, kazanılan para değil.' (insights.savings.disclaimer), 'Zaman değeri, kazanç değil.' (insights.savings.compactDisclaimer), 'Bir gelir kaynağı değildir.' (onboarding.hourlyWage.disclaimer), 'Kaybedilen para değil.' (onboarding.withoutMoneyfesting.fourthLine). forbidden is empty because no tr variant has shipped; the first batch that writes a second wording makes it a forbidden row.

hourly_rate.note: The rate the user sets to price their own time; the source says hourly wage or hourly rate. Keys: onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description. 'maaş' (salary) is forbidden because the app pays nobody, and 'saatlik kazanç' is forbidden because it is also a money-outcome word (references/locale-briefs/tr.md '## Money frame'). Whole-word matching means the badge name proposed for 'Salaried', 'Maaşlı', is not a hit; a badge whose name were the bare 'Maaş' would be, and should be renamed rather than exempted.

goal.note: Apple's Turkish for the daily activity goal is 'hedef' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/1750MoveGoals/localization | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_DESCRIPTION, 'Günlük Hareket Hedefinize 1750 kez ulaşın'). Covers the daily_focus_goal concept: onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*. forbidden is deliberately empty: 'amaç' would be the obvious preventive ban, but it is the right Turkish word for the personal aspiration in onboarding.personalGoal.* ('What are you making time for?'), which concepts.json separates from the daily goal, so a blanket ban would flag correct copy. The list cannot cover every possessive-plus-case stack Turkish produces around a compound such as 'günlük odak hedefindeki'.

minute_unit.note: Foundation on macOS 15.7.9 (24G830) gives tr_TR abbreviated '45 dk.' and narrow '45d'; the brief takes 'dk' without the period because the app's unit is a bare suffix glued to a number, and narrow 'd' is unreadable beside 'g' for gün on the same share card. Spaced '%lld dk' in running text and labels (share.duration.minutesOnly, component.templateTaskCard.duration, achievements.gauge.sessionMinutes, achievements.badge.progressMinutes); tight '%llddk' in width-limited widget and report lines (widgets.streak.focusedInStreak, widgets.streak.focusedMinutesSummary, screenTimeReport.durationMinutesOnly, screenTimeReport.durationUnderOneMinute). Bare unit keys: common.durationMinuteUnit, insights.sessions.durationMinuteUnit, widgets.startFocus.minuteUnit; insights.focus.minutesUnit is uppercase by design and takes 'DK'. Hours are 'sa', seconds 'sn', days 'g'. 'dk.' with a period is not forbidden, because a sentence that ends in the unit legitimately produces it. Accessibility strings spell the unit out ('%lld dakika') and are exempt.

screen_time.note: Apple's Turkish name for the feature (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Screen Time; System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ScreenTimeControllerTitle; support.apple.com/tr-tr/guide/iphone/iphbfa595995/ios, fetched 2026-09-16). 18 en keys. What the list cannot cover: Turkish uses the same two words for the generic 'hours on screen', and term_audit matches case-insensitively, so the glossary cannot separate the feature from the generic sense; the distinction is capitals plus the apostrophe on suffixes and lives in the brief's '## Platform terms' row. The forbidden rows are the English name, the common mistranslation 'Ekran Zamanı', and the straight-apostrophe spellings: Apple writes the suffix separator as U+2019 ('Ekran Süresi’ne'), so a U+0027 is a wrong glyph, not a variant.

Cancel.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Cancel = Vazgeç; NanoTimeKit.framework | NTKCustomization.strings | PHOTOS_CROP_CANCEL = Değişikliklerden Vazgeç. quit is moneyfesting.details.stopConfirmationQuitButton, which ends a running session, so it takes Bitir rather than a word for cancelling a dialog.

Done.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Done and SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | DONE both = Bitti, so the illustrated pill and the app's own button share one form. plan.dailyPlan.doneHeader (en 'DONE') matches the control label case-insensitively but is an uppercase section header, so it gets its own role instead of reading as drift.

Continue.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Continue and FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | COMMON_CONTINUE = Sürdür; ControlCenter/Bundles/TimerModule.bundle | TimerModule.strings | RESUME = Sürdür, so Continue and Resume are one word in Turkish. common.continue is quoted by onboarding.alert.screenTimeMessage and reused by the Screen Time mock, which is why the app-owned CTA keeps Apple's word (open decision continue_label).

Save.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Save = Kaydet. save_money is the literal badge on paywall.onboardingSubscription.annualPlanBadge (en 'Save 56%'), a noun phrase because Turkish puts the percent sign before the number and the badge has no room for a verb; its format-string sibling paywall.plan.annual.savingBadge (en 'SAVE %lld%%') becomes '%%%lld TASARRUF', where the doubled %% produces the literal sign at the head of the string.

Edit.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Edit = Düzenle, but SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | EDIT, the jiggle-mode pill the howTo illustration copies, is literally '+' in Turkish. onboarding.widgets.howTo.editPillLabel mirrors the device, so step2 names the symbol instead of quoting a verb (open decision edit_pill_label).

Delete.note: Apple: UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Delete = Sil. Confirmation questions conjugate ('Bu alıntı silinsin mi?', quotes.user.deleteTitle) and compounds keep the stem ('Tümünü sil', plan.dailyPlan.deleteAll).

Skip.note: Apple: System/Library/BridgeManifests/BridgeManifests.bundle | SettingsSearchManifest-com.apple.watchgestures.bridgesettings.strings | SKIP = Atla. No en key equals 'Skip' exactly; onboarding.name.skip is 'Skip for now'.

Allow.note: Apple: UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | PERMISSION_ALERT_ALLOW; TCC.framework | Localizable.strings | REQUEST_ACCESS_ALLOW. onboarding.notificationPermission.alertAllow mirrors an iOS alert, so the value must equal Apple's.

Don't allow.note: Apple: UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | PERMISSION_ALERT_DENY; FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | COMMON_DONT_ALLOW. Both keys (onboarding.notificationPermission.alertDoNotAllow, onboarding.screenTimePermission.alertDoNotAllow) are mock-alert mirrors.

Got it.note: Open decision got_it_label. Apple's own value for 'Got it' is Tamam (Applications/MusicRecognition.app | Localizable.strings | SOUNDS_LIKE_ALERT_DISMISS; PodcastsFoundation.framework | Localizable.strings | NOW_PLAYING_SCROLLING_TIP_DONE_BUTTON_TITLE), which the six OK keys already take; 'Anladım' keeps the two controls distinct in the same flow.

Retry.note: Apple: _JetEngine_SwiftUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ACTION_RETRY = Yeniden Dene (bare stem); SpringBoard.app | SpringBoard.strings | ACTIVATION_FAILED_RETRY_BUTTON = Yeniden Deneyin (siz imperative). The bare stem is the app-owned form; the four 'Try Again' keys take the same word. Inside a sentence the quoted label takes a following noun rather than a suffix: '„Yeniden Dene” düğmesine dokun' (component.errorView.message).

Settings.note: Apple: Preferences.app | InfoPlist.strings | CFBundleDisplayName = Ayarlar; SpringBoard.app | SpringBoard.strings | FACE_ID_DISABLED_GO_TO_SETTINGS = Ayarlar’ı Aç; ScreenTimeAppIntentsExtension.appex | Localizable.strings | Go to Settings = Ayarlar’a Git. Turkish distinguishes the two buttons where Romanian merges them, so goto_button is a tr-only role name: insights.appUsage.openSettings and share.alert.openSettings take open_button, onboarding.alert.goToSettings and theme.picker.goToSettingsButton take goto_button. The suffix separator is U+2019, per TDK's kesme işareti rule (tdk.gov.tr/icerik/yazim-kurallari/kesme-isareti/, fetched 2026-09-16).

open.recommended_reason: Apple itself switches to sen exactly where its Turkish copy congratulates and coaches, which is what this app's streak, badge and widget lines do.
open.note: Keys: every reader-directed string; the hotspots are the 177 en second-person possessives, the 15 celebration and badge 'earned' lines, and onboarding.age.title / onboarding.personalGoal.title. Rule: the app's voice is a friendly coach, but a string that mirrors an iOS alert or quotes an iOS label follows the device. Evidence for sen: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/365AllGoals/localization | Localizable-Modified-tinker.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_PROGRESS_THREE_AWAY_DESC/NSStringLocalizedFormatKey ('Halkalarını üç gün daha kapatıp harika bir ödül kazan!'). Evidence for siz: UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE ('Size Bildirimler Göndermek İstiyor'); HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable.strings | AUTHORIZATION_DONT_ALLOW_ALERT_MESSAGE ('açabilirsiniz'); support.apple.com/tr-tr/guide/iphone/iphbfa595995/ios (fetched 2026-09-16). Meanwhile: app-owned copy uses sen, mirrors stay verbatim Apple with siz, and the adjudicator lists every key that turned on the choice. term_audit counts the bare pronouns, which UI copy rarely writes; the real check is the brief's grep aid on the siz endings ınız|iniz|unuz|ünüz|sınız|siniz|sunuz|sünüz.

open.recommended_reason: In an app's interface 'oturum' first reads as a login session, while this product's session is a timed block of activity, which is what 'seans' names in everyday Turkish.
open.note: Keys: widgets.startFocus.heading, moneyfesting.details.*, insights.sessions.*, profile.sessionDetails.*, focusTask.*. Evidence for odak oturumu: Apple renders Session as Oturum (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SensorKitUI.framework/AuthGroups/ECG.bundle | InfoPlist.strings | Session). Evidence against it in UI: the same runtime uses oturum for a sign-in session (System/Library/CoreServices/SpringBoard.app | SpringBoard.strings | LOGOUT_TEMPORARY_SESSION_LOGOUT_ALERT_TITLE, 'Oturum Bitirilsin mi?'). The base noun is settled either way: Apple names the system Focus mode 'Odak' (Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Focus; ControlCenter/Bundles/FocusUIModule.bundle | Localizable.strings | MODULE_DEFAULT_TITLE), and no app key names the system mode, so there is no collision to avoid. Meanwhile: new strings use 'odak seansı' and the adjudicator lists every key that touched the term; a flip is a global term change with its own follow-up batch, never a per-string choice.

open.recommended_reason: The inventory copy counts earned items, and a countable 'dondurma hakkı' reads naturally while 'koruma' loses the connection to the frozen day drawn on the week strip.
open.note: Keys: streakFreeze.* (info.title, info.available, info.automatic, inventoryAccessibility, ready, noneAvailable, usedBody, dayAccessibility, info.accessibilityHint), paywall.benefit.streak.detail, widgets.streak.copy.frozen.*, widgets.streak.a11y.frozen. Rule: a freeze covers one missed day, never two (catalog comment on paywall.benefit.streak.detail), whichever word wins. Evidence for seri dondurma: 'dondurma' is the standard Turkish word for suspending a membership or an account; out of context it is also the word for ice cream, which is the argument against it. Evidence for seri koruması: it states the mechanic with no second reading, but it drops the image the widget art carries. No Apple string covers this concept: a runtime search for 'Freeze' returned no Turkish UI label. Meanwhile: new strings use 'seri dondurma' / 'dondurma hakkı'.

open.recommended_reason: The how-to steps tell the reader to find menu items that say 'Araç Takımı Ekle' on their own phone, so a screen that teaches the menu in a different word is the one place the mismatch is certain to be seen.
open.note: Keys: the 13 en widget keys (onboarding.widgets.howTo.chooseTitle, .editTitle, .step4, .subtitle, onboarding.widgets.intro.appIconInstruction, onboarding.welcome.preview.streak.homeScreen, onboarding.welcome.slide.streak.eyebrow, profile.home.widgetsRow) plus every widgets.*.displayName and .description. Rule: Apple product and feature names take Apple's own localization. Evidence for araç takımı: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | WIDGET, EDIT_MENU_ADD_WIDGET, REMOVE_WIDGET_SHORTCUT_ITEM_TITLE; SmartStackSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | SMART_STACK_SUGGESTION_SETTINGS_WIDGETS_SECTION_HEADER ('Araç Takımları'). Evidence for widget: it is the loanword Turkish speakers use in conversation and it is far shorter on a gallery description under a width budget. Meanwhile: the onboarding.widgets.howTo.*Label family uses 'araç takımı' whatever happens, because those values are verbatim mirrors; other new strings follow the recommendation.

open.recommended_reason: Both keys end an explanation the reader has just finished, and 'Tamam' would make two different controls share one label inside the same flow.
open.note: Keys: onboarding.widgets.howTo.continueButton, streakFreeze.info.done. Rule: an app-owned control defaults to Apple's wording for a matching control. Evidence for Tamam: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, Applications/MusicRecognition.app | Localizable.strings | SOUNDS_LIKE_ALERT_DISMISS and System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/PodcastsFoundation.framework | Localizable.strings | NOW_PLAYING_SCROLLING_TIP_DONE_BUTTON_TITLE both render 'Got It' as Tamam. Evidence for Anladım: Apple's Tamam is also its value for OK (UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | OK), which the app already needs on six keys (common.ok, insights.mood.ok, quotes.user.okay, onboarding.alert.ok and two literals). Meanwhile: controls['Got it'] is Anladım and common.ok stays Tamam.

open.recommended_reason: It costs no new key, keeps the instruction that tells the user which button to tap literally correct, and is already the word the device shows on that button.
open.note: Keys: common.continue, achievements.action.continue, insights.appUsage.allowAccess, paywall.button.subscribe; onboarding.alert.screenTimeMessage quotes common.continue, and the Screen Time mock reuses it. Rule: a string that quotes an iOS alert equals Apple's value. Evidence for Sürdür: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Continue and Applications/FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | COMMON_CONTINUE. Evidence for Devam et: it is the everyday Turkish CTA, and 'Sürdür' literally means carry on, which reads oddly on a subscribe button; choosing it costs a Continue key of its own for the mock and the quoted instruction, which is a code change. Meanwhile: 'Sürdür' everywhere, and common.continue is never split without the owner.

open.recommended_reason: VoiceOver reads the forecast line and the month-end figure one after the other, and 'Öngörü' keeps them audibly distinct while 'Ay sonu tahmini' keeps the estimate word for the figure.
open.note: Keys: insights.savings.forecast (en 'Forecast'), insights.savings.monthEnd (en 'Month-end estimate'), insights.savings.estimateExplanation, .measuredEstimateExplanation, .focusHistoryEstimateExplanation, insights.appUsage.permissionDescription. Rule: the forecast line and the month-end figure stay two different words whatever is chosen, and neither becomes a promise (the concept is an estimate with a stated formula). Evidence: 'Tahmin' shares its stem with 'tahmini', which the month-end label needs, so the two adjacent labels would repeat; 'Projeksiyon' is a loanword that reads as a technical term beside plain copy. No Apple string covers a month-end money forecast. Meanwhile: new strings use 'Öngörü' for the line and 'Ay sonu tahmini' for the figure.

open.recommended_reason: The illustration exists to look like the reader's own Home Screen, and a word on that pill would send them looking for something their phone does not show.
open.note: Keys: onboarding.widgets.howTo.editPillLabel (drawn at Manifesting/Features/Onboarding/Business/WidgetsHowTo/View/HomeScreenJiggleIllustrationView.swift) and onboarding.widgets.howTo.step2, which quotes it. Rule: an illustrated iOS label mirrors the device verbatim. Evidence: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | EDIT is literally '+' in tr.lproj, where ro.lproj has 'Editați' and en has 'Edit'. Consequence: step2 cannot quote a verb and must name the symbol instead ('Sağ üst köşedeki + düğmesine dokun, sonra Araç Takımı Ekle’yi seç.'), which is app copy and needs no code change. Meanwhile: the label mirrors Apple and step2 names the symbol; a render check of the pill at the illustration's width is required before shipping either option.

Rule: illustrated labels and the steps that quote them mirror the device verbatim. open.recommended_reason: The apostrophe form is correct Turkish for a fixed proper name and leaves the brand letters untouched, while a suffix on a %@ placeholder cannot be harmonised at runtime.
open.note: Keys: the 40 en units that carry the brand (2 of them key literals), including main.tab.moneyfesting, insights.sessions.title, streakFreeze.info.title, share.text.fromTheApp, insights.mood.permissionMessage, share.alert.photoAccessDeniedMessage; plus the app-name placeholder in onboarding.screenTimePermission.alertTitle/.alertMessage/.message, onboarding.notificationPermission.alertTitle and onboarding.widgets.howTo.step3/.searchTitle. Rule: the brand stays exactly as written in every language and script; declension is allowed only in the locale's normal form (references/voice-card.md '## Brand and fixed names'). Evidence for the apostrophe: TDK, 'Özel adlara getirilen iyelik, durum ve bildirme ekleri kesme işaretiyle ayrılır' (tdk.gov.tr/icerik/yazim-kurallari/kesme-isareti/, fetched 2026-09-16); the separator character is U+2019, as Apple writes it in 'Ayarlar’ı Aç'. Evidence for the noun pattern: Apple puts a common noun after a placeholder rather than suffixing it, iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL ('“%@” uygulamasına … erişim izni verme'). Meanwhile: never glue a suffix to the brand without the apostrophe, and never suffix a placeholder.

open.recommended_reason: 'b' is not a neutral abbreviation in Turkish: 'B' is the locale's own compact token for bin, a value a thousand times smaller than the billions the app means by it.
open.note: Not a wording choice: an engineering finding to report, never something a translation run edits or writes around. AppCurrency.formatCompact appends a hardcoded Latin 'k'/'m'/'b' (Manifesting/Foundation/Localization/AppCurrency.swift:54-56), producing 'TRY\u00a01,25b'; Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency(code:locale:).notation(.compactName) for tr_TR gives '1,25\u00a0B\u00a0TRY' and '1,25\u00a0Mn\u00a0TRY', and the plain number style gives '1,25 Mr' for billions (Foundation on macOS 15.7.9 (24G830)). Reached from FocusRingCopy.swift:25, MonthlyTimeValueTile.swift:53,68, InsightsSavingsCard.swift:36,46 and ScreenTimeUsageReportViews.swift:126,251, plus the insights, celebration, details and session screens. Visible figures are compact while accessibility labels use the full format, so review both.
